blocks.body: Courtyard creates owner value on select-service conversions where Bonvoy distribution and a proven business-travel product can stabilize demand—sponsors underwrite lobby, F&B, and guestroom PIP so affiliation is not modeled as a light cosmetic reflag.

blocks.title: Data & Analytics
blocks.body: Parent revenue and CRM analytics support Courtyard by Marriott where connected—property teams still own local competitive response.

blocks.title: Corporate Corridor Portfolio Play
blocks.body: Corporate and airport corridors fit Courtyard when transient demand is durable and capital can deliver consistent select-service standards—owners gain Marriott channel scale when labor and brand presentation stay inside corridor underwriting.

blocks.title: International Demand
blocks.body: International feed depends on Marriott Bonvoy awareness and source-market airlift—do not assume global portfolio strength equals this hotel's inbound mix.

blocks.title: Purpose-Built New Development
blocks.body: New-build Courtyard projects suit sponsors who want a disciplined select-service prototype rather than full-service capital—value holds when construction costs, operator readiness, and Bonvoy economics are modeled to realistic rate-positioning peers.

blocks.title: Leisure & Destination
blocks.body: Leisure fit follows whether Courtyard by Marriott's product matches destination seasonality and amenity expectations.

blocks.title: Third-Party Operator-Led
blocks.body: Courtyard works with operators who can execute Marriott brand standards and select-service rhythms—sponsors need Bonvoy lift and financing credibility while conversion or prototype scope, staffing, and F&B intensity stay inside underwriting.

blocks.title: Reputation & QA
blocks.body: Guest scores and brand QA affect ranking in Marriott Bonvoy search and account eligibility—budget reputation management.
